A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same eNCP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M support reliable comparison despite the changed title, formatting, and expanded material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic conditional-distribution experiments, robot momentum regression, and uncertainty estimates for simulated quadruped locomotion, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds synthetic regression, symmetry-misspecification experiments, augmentation comparisons, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix E changes the specified trainable operator blocks from scalar coefficient matrices tensored with identity matrices to sums over real, complex, or quaternionic endomorphism bases. Appendix F.2 correspondingly revises the regularization calculation. This substantially broadens the permitted operator parameterization, while retaining the two encoders and overall contrastive-learning framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds one-dimensional regression and uncertainty quantification with skewed, symmetric, and bimodal heteroscedastic conditionals, plus scenarios involving asymmetric sampling support and incorrect conditional symmetries (Appendices G.4–G.5). The existing cGMM and robotics tasks remain. The bivariate synthetic quantile task also gains negative-input coverage.

E2.justification: v3 introduces NCP with data augmentation, NCPaug, as an evaluated comparator in the synthetic regression and convergence comparisons, particularly Figure 15. The comparator sets in the retained operator-learning, robot-regression, and robotics uncertainty experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The synthetic quantile generator changes from x uniform on [0.8,3.2] to uniform on [-4,-0.8] union [0.8,4], using |x| in the response law. New protocols include a 20,000-pair regression benchmark, coverage sweeps, regional error measurements under controlled misspecification, and timing comparisons. The original 70/15/15 splits remain. The revised generator description alone does not establish that retained plots were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the earlier invariance and learned-basis analyses, v3 compares architectural symmetry with data augmentation and examines convergence (Figure 15), calibration across coverage levels (Figure 14), and sensitivity to sampling, noise, and conditional-mean misspecification (Figures 16–18). Appendix G.7 additionally analyzes computational costs across symmetry groups.

E5.justification: v1 shows uncertainty bands and plus/minus results without specifying seed counts. v3 Appendix G discloses three to five random seeds for sample-efficiency experiments, and Table 5 specifies mean and standard deviation over 200 post-warmup passes. These disclosures do not establish increased replication of the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds calibration, convergence, and misspecification findings, including improved extrapolation under asymmetric sampling and increasing conditional-mean error under incorrect symmetry. Table 5 newly reports 3.2–5.6 times NCP's forward-training cost and approximately 1.1–1.2 times its inference cost. The existing robotics values in Table 4 are unchanged; their set-size entries are additionally displayed in Table 2.

T1.justification: Appendices I and K distinguish complex Schur theory from real representations, introduce endomorphism and singular-space results, and revise the operator/SVD derivations. Quotient groups are formally defined through irreducible-representation kernels. Theorem 5.1 revises the rank prescription and logarithmic factor, while Table 1 changes the loss-to-representation-error bound. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The principal claims about eNCP, task-agnostic inference, statistical guarantees, and robotics performance remain. The abstract refines the claimed disentangled structure from independent symmetry subgroups to quotient groups, changing its mathematical meaning without redefining the overall contribution.

C2.justification: v1 largely leaves symmetry misspecification to future work. v3 distinguishes useful regularization under sampling asymmetry from failures under incorrect conditional symmetries, explains training and inference tradeoffs, and explicitly acknowledges that representation-learning error lacks a full statistical characterization. Appendix E.1 also discusses applicability to continuous and noncompact symmetry settings.

D1.justification: v3 documents quantile-transformer binning, concrete architecture and regularization settings for the new regression experiment, and implementation helpers for isotypic decomposition and changing representation bases. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named repository and identifies an additional implementation library. These are focused reproducibility and access improvements.

R1.justification: v3 adds relevant mathematical and implementation references and refines its positioning against Behboodi et al.'s equivariant-network generalization bounds by distinguishing classification from regression and uncertainty quantification. Wang et al. (2023) supplies the misspecification taxonomy. The broader positioning between contrastive learning and geometric deep learning remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the method and guarantee exposition, brings encoder-parameterization explanations into the main text, and restructures the representation-theory and experimental appendices. It also expands navigation, revises terminology and captions, and shortens the title. These changes extend beyond inserting new scientific material.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. v3 adds calibration, convergence, robustness, and endomorphism figures plus the runtime table. Existing displays are also expanded or redistributed: Table 2 gains previously reported set sizes, and Figure 5 brings part of the retained appendix ground-force visualization into the main text.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves assessment of the method's applicability: it tests the central symmetry assumption under several controlled violations instead of leaving robustness entirely to future work. Augmentation comparisons and timing measurements expose practical benefits and costs, while expanded operator theory and explicit qualifications clarify the guarantees. Reporting inconsistencies remain, including the robotics experiments' 90% versus 95% targets, but the added diagnostics and transparency provide a substantial overall gain.
